Two different model families, two different thinking-mode configurations, and two very different load conditions all produced the same narrow duration/token-count band - this is inconsistent with a pure compute-throughput explanation and points to something structural in the AnythingLLM<->Ollama tool-calling wire protocol/timeout handling for this MCP tool-schema setup (AnythingLLM 1.16.1, Ollama 0.33.2), not a model capability or resource-availability limitation.

AnythingLLM registers MCP tools under a PREFIXED name, <mcpServerName>-<toolName> (confirmed live: "world-server-sandbox-read_text_file", not "read_text_file"). AnythingLLM constructs its own outbound `ollama` client with a custom fetch ONLY if process.env.OLLAMA_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT is set to a valid number >= 300000ms (5 minutes); if that env var is unset (the default on this machine), it falls straight back to the plain global `fetch`, which under Node/undici carries a default headersTimeout of exactly 300000ms (5 minutes) on the dispatcher used for AnythingLLM's own request TO Ollama. This is a completely separate timeout from scripts/anythingllm-task-router.cjs's own client-side AbortSignal.timeout (600000ms) - AnythingLLM's own outbound call to Ollama was dying at ~5 minutes, long before our own 10-minute client timeout would ever fire. This is the true explanation for both live 'error_fetch failed' incidents (job 3877989c...f2acdaa and simple-e2e run1: wallClockMs 306464, i.e. ~5m6s - the ~6s of overhead is AnythingLLM's own pre-processing/resource checks before the actual Ollama chat() call starts). Note the previously-recorded durationMs:600000 on both incidents was NOT a real measurement - scripts/anythingllm-task-router.cjs's catch block for a thrown fetch error hardcodes `durationMs: timeoutMs` (the configured constant) rather than computing real elapsed time, which is itself a minor observability bug worth fixing separately but did not affect the classification fix in #anythingllm-transient-dispatch-failure-terminally-failed, which remains correct and necessary regardless of the exact failure cause.
